campaign: GUI capability roadmap: flat conversation workflow, reachable workspaces, correct serving contracts and the training loop in the workbench
doctrine:
Owner direction, 2026-09-13: the roadmap now also covers reachability of Train, Model Builder and Evaluations in the documented launch; correctness of the serving contracts the workbench depends on (declared sampler chain, credential-less GET admission, native video routes, Library validation with a projector); workbench consumers for capabilities that have none (inference sessions, agent recovery and streaming tools, model merge, declared speculative decoding); the workbench side of the training loop (conversation dataset preview, adapter training served from the picker, run export, preference training); and the style floor Impeccable's craft floor, audit, typeset, harden and clarify references describe (C:/Users/jeffm/impeccable, read-only concept source), applied after functionality is verified and only as measurements the browser lane computes and ratchets, never as review prose. Training internals, converters, objectives and their evidence stay master-owned under the train-serve-loop reference row; a lane row that consumes them waits for the master step it names. Each new row binds its own browser journey marker and, where it changes a server contract, a file-guarded owning-package test; local signoff requires every marker. No new model family, optimizer or orchestration framework; derive adapter rank, draft depth and chain defaults from declarations rather than entering them.

Current owner direction: merge master into professional_overgo_gui while retaining this plan, then continue with the next GUI capability. Work exclusively in this worktree. Publishing subsequent GUI changes into master requires separate owner authorization.

Preserve the conversation-first design: flat messages, lists and separators; no cards; independently scrolling messages; reachable Send/Stop; one compact model selector with explicit details; mobile navigation drawer; settings on demand; status only for relevant progress, failure or required action. Keep the embedded same-origin client, CSP, authenticated shared transport and existing workbench/state owners. Apply Impeccable guidance to clarity, focus, typography and touch behavior after functionality is verified.

Prevent lost drafts, incorrect cancellation and hidden device capture. Responses, lineage, operations, artifacts, admission and decisions remain server-owned. Browser drafts/settings exclude secrets and captured bytes. Distinguish Stop from disconnect, resume from retry, branch creation from mutation, shared memory admission from exclusive measurement reservations, and recorded attachments from live streams. Reuse existing transactions, evidence handles and abandoned-admission recovery.

Master is integrated through 08cbbd5142e9 (2026-09-13, the third integration that day): retained gate costs are queryable through plan history, imported Go types are reused within each census, generic CLI helpers no longer depend on inference or the CUDA driver (the served child types its own device-memory exit), the preparation census is computed once, the gate reports actual per-package verification cost and bounds each active test instead of the suite duration, publication cost is measured against retained gate attempts, instruction evaluation progress persists across resumption, and Qwen4 and Qwen9 native instruction validation is complete; exact artifact identity in model selection, declared chat framing and selected model evidence stay preserved. The master-owned reference rows mirror master's open plan at that revision (publication cost, gate selection, modality verification, regression, benchmark, recovery and simplification); the lane never dispatches them, and a lane row that needs master's work names the master step it waits on. Native NDJSON transcription streaming now has production session/checkpoint owners; browser live input still needs a compatible bounded transport and source-identity contract. CPU and server tests do not prove browser live streaming, physical-phone operation, model understanding or held-out quality.

Only professional_overgo_gui rows are local work. Retain master-owned historical identities, dependencies and verifier floors as coordination references; reconcile their disposition in master before execution. The 27B benchmark remains operator-launched. The four inherited audio/training surface obligations remain under audio-staged-surface pending owner's reconciliation; no parallel audio backend.

Future named browser tests are implementation obligations, not present evidence. Assert actual actions, encoded bytes, request/terminal state and cleanup. Preserve existing GUI regression floors. Use synthetic devices and fixtures for focused acceptance, then the full real-model lane for local signoff. Separate physical iOS/Android/Safari/screen-reader evidence from Chromium emulation; missing hardware stays outstanding and does not block implementable local rows. Gate commits through cmd/gate. Bind inherited audio and smoke reference fixtures read-only; keep general data root and browser writes local to this worktree. No arbitrary source-size ceilings or silently skipped supported cases.

items.title: Refuse cross-site side-effecting GET requests at the shared admission

steps.title: Refuse cross-site side-effecting GET requests at the shared admission
steps.verify: test -f internal/apimanifest/admission_get_test.go && go test ./internal/apimanifest -run '^TestCredentiallessGETSideEffects$' -count=1 && test -f internal/modelswap/proxy_cross_site_test.go && go test ./internal/modelswap -run '^TestProxyRefusesCrossSiteSwap$' -count=1
steps.rationale: AdmitCredentialless relies on net/http CrossOriginProtection, which admits GET, HEAD and OPTIONS before any Origin or Sec-Fetch-Site check (internal/apimanifest/admission.go:40-43). The proxy honours ?swap= on GET, which is the model pill's own path, so a foreign page can launch or swap a model; GET /library/providers/models takes endpoint and key_environment from the query and the intake sends the named environment variable as a bearer token to that endpoint. SECURITY.md states neither is possible. Require a same-origin Sec-Fetch-Site or the bearer key for every GET with a side effect, or move those effects to POST, keep the same-origin workbench working, and correct SECURITY.md in the same batch. Acceptance: cross-site GET swap and provider listing are refused without any mutation; same-origin and authenticated requests pass; the workbench journeys still pass.

items.title: Explain refused workspaces instead of hiding them and release tab resources on remount

steps.title: Explain refused workspaces instead of hiding them and release tab resources on remount
steps.rationale: Refused tabs are removed from the navigation with the reason left in a title attribute, and fragment navigation reaches the refused module anyway (internal/server/webui/boot.js:782-793); safeMount discards module cleanup functions, so SSE streams accumulate on each remount (boot.js:596-597); the Automations tab posts decisions without the approval request identity and receives 409 hidden in an unhandled rejection. Show a refused workspace as a flat status line with its reason and the action that would enable it, refuse fragment navigation to it with the same message, run every module's cleanup on remount, and send the approval identity. Acceptance: the journey opens a refused tab and reads its reason, remounts a streaming tab and observes one live stream, and a decision on a pending approval succeeds.

items.title: Validate a registered model with a projector from the Library, independently of the working directory

steps.title: Validate a registered model with a projector from the Library, independently of the working directory
steps.verify: test -f internal/libraryintake/projector_validation_test.go && go test ./internal/libraryintake -run '^TestValidateTextWithProjector$' -count=1 && go run ./cmd/webui-lane -run '^TestWebUIBrowser(LibraryValidation|LayoutAudit)$' -require 'library validation leg'
steps.rationale: ModelFiles returns a sibling projector automatically and the page posts it back, but Validate refuses any projector before text validation runs (internal/libraryintake/intake.go:81-82, :123-124), so a model downloaded with its mmproj never becomes servable through the Library. library_validation.json is opened relative to the process working directory (internal/server/library_workspace.go:104), CleanRevision refuses any dirty Go file, and the idle shell routes neither /library/validate nor /hub/downloads. Validate text inference when a projector is present, resolve the validation policy from the repository root, and route validation through the idle shell so an empty store reaches a served model. Acceptance: register-plus-validate on a real small GGUF with a projector activates a text recipe; the journey downloads, registers, validates and selects the model from a cold proxy.

items.title: Deliver the declared video output on the native video routes

steps.title: Deliver the declared video output on the native video routes
steps.rationale: Every video executor publishes image/gif (internal/mediacapability/output.go:34-40) and /v1/videos/generations and /v1/videos/edits require a video/ media type (internal/server/native_media_protocols.go:90, :125), so the routes return 500 after the operation has already committed its output; the route tests use a fake video/mp4 artifact. The video-edit task has no executor, so /v1/videos/edits and workflow.video-edit can never execute. Accept the declared output type on the routes, and either give video-edit its executor through the existing LiveEdit reference-edit runtime or retire the task, its route and its workflow declaration in one batch. Acceptance: the route test uses the real executor output type; a video-gen operation's result downloads through the route; video-edit is either exercised or absent from the capability catalog.

items.title: Resume agent sessions after interruption and stream tool output in the thread

steps.title: Resume agent sessions after interruption and stream tool output in the thread
steps.verify: test -f internal/server/agent_session_recovery_test.go && go test ./internal/server -run '^TestAgentSessionRecoveryAndStreaming$' -count=1 && go run ./cmd/webui-lane -run '^TestWebUIBrowser(AgentRecovery|LayoutAudit)$' -require 'agent recovery leg'
steps.rationale: Agent recovery and checkpoints (internal/agentloop/recovery.go) and the streaming NDJSON tool transport have no production caller; operations are in-memory and evictable (internal/operation/runtime.go:526-543), so a server restart loses the session the README promises to recover. Persist agent sessions and their receipts through the existing interaction store, restore them on startup, and carry tool output through the duplex transport into the thread as it arrives. Acceptance: a session interrupted mid-tool resumes after restart without duplicating the tool effect; streamed tool output appears incrementally; approvals survive the restart.

items.title: Measure the Impeccable craft floor in the browser lane at every state, viewport and scheme

steps.title: Measure the Impeccable craft floor in the browser lane at every state, viewport and scheme
steps.verify: test -f internal/webuilane/craft_floor_test.go && go test ./internal/webuilane -run '^TestCraftFloorTokenContrast$' -count=1 && go run ./cmd/webui-lane -run '^TestWebUIBrowser(CraftFloor|LayoutAudit)$' -require 'craft floor leg'
steps.rationale: The layout audit that CaptureStates runs at desktop and phone under dark and light already measures horizontal overflow, overlapping surfaces, clipped text and AA contrast. Extend it with the rest of the floor Impeccable verifies on the built result, as computed measurements rather than review notes: no text below the smallest type token (the .sub label renders at 8.5px today); interactive targets at or above 44 CSS pixels on the phone viewport; a visible focus indicator on every focusable element; a heading hierarchy without skipped levels; easing functions without overshoot; placeholder text at body contrast; and, under emulated prefers-reduced-motion, state changes that still complete, which the current global 0.01ms transition kill does not guarantee for streamed status. Findings are a ratchet baseline the way the composer budget is: the count only falls. Acceptance: the token contrast test computes every text-on-surface pair for both themes from style.css; the browser journey audits every captured state and its baseline holds; a seeded 40px target and a seeded 9px label fail.

items.title: Set one role scale and reading measure for an operate surface and remove the eyebrow label

steps.title: Set one role scale and reading measure for an operate surface and remove the eyebrow label
steps.rationale: Impeccable's typeset guidance for an operate-and-read surface is one well-tuned family with a fixed role scale; the craft floor sets the reading measure at 65 to 75 characters and bans the kicker or eyebrow above a heading outright. The workbench keeps its system family by that rule, recorded as the decision rather than a default, and fixes what the rule finds: the conversation and composer share a 720px measure, which at the 14px body is beyond 75ch; the .sub pill is an uppercase letter-spaced eyebrow at 8.5px; role sizes are pinned in pixels with no fluid step between phone and desktop. Derive the measure from the body size, give each type token one role, and delete the eyebrow. Acceptance: the journey measures the reading width in characters at both viewports, finds no uppercase tracked label above a heading, and finds every text node on a token size.

items.title: Prove every workspace under extreme input, empty, loading and failure states with copy that names the recovery

steps.title: Prove every workspace under extreme input, empty, loading and failure states with copy that names the recovery
steps.rationale: Impeccable's harden, clarify and onboard checks are journeys, not styling: names of 100+ characters, emoji, CJK and RTL text, a thousand-row list, ten rapid submits, forced request failures, and every workspace with no data. Each state must render without clipped or overflowing text, keep Send and Stop reachable, and show copy that states what failed and how to recover or what to do first; an empty workspace names what will appear there and the action that creates it. Reuse the existing conversation, attachment and background-work journeys for the inputs and add the extreme-input and empty-state passes. Acceptance: the journey feeds each input class to each workspace at both viewports and both schemes, the layout audit reports no overflow or clipping, and every failure and empty state carries an action.
